transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2029-01-15 16:00 UTC / Duration: ~60m / Attendees: Alex Monroe, Priya Shah, Diego Ramos (Redwood); Jordan Lee, Paula Mendes, Samir Patel, Maya Huang (Vireo)

Summary (auto): QBR-style checkin focusing on runway and sprint handoff. Customer wants predictable billing and lower per-token cost for 'assistant' flows. Redwood proposes Dedicated pilot with autoscale cap + fallback to hosted.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda — cost velocity, pilot scope, security handoff, and then open q's. Jordan can you kick off with current usage?
00:24 Jordan: yeah, thanks Alex. So, last quarter we ramped the assistant feature, we're seeing peaks at 3k rps for short-form prompts but it's bursty, like 10x every hour, and that is where our token burn spikes. We also pushed a new prompt set for summarization.
00:48 Priya: got it, so 3k rps spikes, what's typical sequence lengths and kv cache reuse? are you hitting long context?
01:10 Jordan: most are sub-200 tokens, but conversational retention means kv-caching matters; we think existing caching isn't working great with our layer, maybe we're invalidating too often, so KV cache reuse is low.
01:33 Paula: yes we flush caches on session end for security reasons, but we can explore sliding windows or session pinning.
01:46 Alex: okay that ties into batching and quantization recommendations — if avg seq len is low, batching helps a lot. Also we probably can suggest a quant profile for the summarization model to cut cost ~15-30% with <1% quality loss.
02:05 Samir: wait when you say 15-30% that's per-token cost? can you give a monthly projection if we moved 40% of traffic to Dedicated?
02:18 Alex: we'll send a modelled projection; rough back-of-envelope: Dedicated reserved (8 GPUs) with smarter batching+caching could cut unit cost ~35% compared to hosted variable pricing for sustained traffic — but commit terms and burst handling matter. We'll email the spreadsheet.
02:40 Jordan: timeline — we want pilot before end of Feb, ideally.
02:48 Priya: technically doable; pilot scope: 2-week benchmark + 6-week soft launch on Dedicated with canary routing and fallback to hosted. Runbook will include autoscale caps and cost triggers.
03:12 Paula: network/security question — can we run Private (VPC) option? we need SSO, RBAC, KMS integration, audit logs.
03:28 Priya: yes, VPC private control plane is supported; we integrate with customer KMS (bring-your-own) for at-rest key management, SAML SSO is supported, and we can retain audit logs to your SIEM. I'll share the network diagram.
03:49 Jordan: how about SOC2/ISO attestation? our sec team will want the report.
03:56 Diego: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 packages, I'll drop the evidence link after the call, and the security whitepaper.
04:08 Maya: any risk around PII in prompts? we need redaction guidance or options to not persist raw prompts.
04:18 Priya: you can enable prompt redaction and policy filters; also we support ephemeral cache modes where we do not persist raw inputs beyond transit. We should align on retention window.
04:35 Samir: finance: Overage triggers — if Dedicated cap is hit, who pays for fallback? need clear SLA and overage handling.
04:48 Alex: we propose a fallback policy: during pilot, overflow goes to hosted and we log costs itemized; for production we'll include overage thresholds and pre-approved burst credits as part of contract. We'll include explicit billing rules in the pilot contract.
05:05 Jordan: ok that sounds reasonable.
05:12 Priya: technical deep-dive note: for quantization we need to ensure your model variant is compliant; if you want to use 4-bit quant we may need extra evals. Also kernel optimizations vary by GPU family.
05:33 Paula: we run NV-series GPUs on prem, but for dedicated Redwood pool we want to match performance — any profiler we can run?
05:44 Priya: we'll run a micro-benchmark agent; we'll request a docker container with the model, or you can run our client harness. We'll do perf numbers on the target sequence lengths.
06:05 Jordan: important: we have regulatory customers in EU — data residency required for some tenants. Can we route those to EU region?
06:18 Diego: yes routing policies by region and model version are supported, we can create a route that pins EU tenants to EU Dedicated pool.
06:30 Samir: also, what about support SLAs? we need 4-hour P1 and a named escalation path.
06:40 Alex: enterprise package includes 4-hour P1, 24/7 on-call for Sev1 during launch; we'll share the escalation playbook.
06:50 Maya: quick question about model rollouts — we want A/B test between two instruction-tuned variants. Is rollout builtin?
07:02 Priya: yes we have canary and A/B routing with automatic fallback and traffic shadowing; you can also use per-prompt eval sets in the Console to monitor regressions.
07:22 Jordan: one more: our team has seen occasional latency spikes during large batch windows; how do you mitigate tail latency?
07:34 Priya: we do continuous batching with latency SLOs and we can pin a small low-latency pool for critical endpoints. Also prefix/KV caching reduces load. You can set a policy to prioritize latency over cost for certain routes.
07:57 Samir: is there a way to simulate cost impact of changing cache policy?
08:06 Alex: yes, we'll produce a cost-sensitivity chart based on your traffic profile. We'll include scenarios: aggressive caching, moderate caching, no caching.
08:20 Paula: note — our infra team will need the VPC peering steps documented, and firewall ports.
08:28 Priya: I'll attach a step-by-step with ip ranges and ports; also we support private link if peering isn't viable.
08:41 Jordan: do you have any runbook for incident response e.g., model hallucination or prompt injection?
08:50 Diego: yes, incident playbooks for safety regressions and misbehavior are in our handbook; we'll share sanitized examples.
09:05 Maya: ok great. Can we recap next steps?
09:10 Alex: recap: Redwood sends pilot pricing spreadsheet + contract draft (Alex), Priya shares SOC2/ISO + VPC diagram + runbook (Priya), Diego sets dashboard access and retention (Diego), Paula uploads traffic CSV and sample prompts (Paula).
09:30 Samir: finance will need a clear monthly forecast with overage scenarios; please call that out in the spreadsheet.
09:41 Alex: noted. We'll also propose a two-week benchmark window where Redwood and Vireo will run identical prompts to compare latency and cost.
09:56 Jordan: sounds good, plan to reconvene after pilot results.
10:05 Paula: one small point — we may want a pre-signed NDA addendum for some logs; legal will follow up.
10:14 Alex: that's fine, Diego and I will sync with legal.

Auto-generated Action Items (end): see action_items field.

Closing (final 2m): casual wrap up, thanks, and Alex drops link: security docs will be shared to security@vireo.com and I'll create calendar invite for benchmark window.

Notes on transcription: some technical terms were imperfectly transcribed (KV cache sometimes as K V cash, SOC2 as SOC two). Occasional crosstalk and truncation.

Explicit next meeting: bench run kickoff - tentative 2029-01-23 14:00 UTC (to be confirmed).

End of transcript.
